---
order: 5
unit: drawing
introduces: [variable-update]
title: A value that grows
summary: A variable can change itself, so a value grows each time round a loop.
language: python
hook: "Scores go up, timers count down and bank balances change. All of them are a variable that works out its next value from its last one."
app:
  command: "node \"$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs\" \"$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground\" 8123"
  url: "http://127.0.0.1:8123/index.html"
  ready: Python code
  layout: full
voice: true
explainClip:
  query: { code: "", speed: 8 }
  caption: "A variable can change itself"
  say: "A variable can work out its next value from its last one."
  pacing: { keyDelayMs: 22 }
  clip:
    - type: { into: "Python code", text: "from turtle import *\n\nsize = 0\n\nfor i in range(30):\n    forward(size)\n    right(90)\n", append: true }
    - caption:
        text: "size = size + 5 works out size + 5, then stores it back in size."
        say: "Work out size plus five, then store the answer back in size."
    - type: { into: "Python code", text: "    size = size + 5\n", append: true }
    - click: "Run"
    - caption:
        text: "size grows by 5 every pass, so the lines grow."
        say: "Size grows by five every pass, so the lines grow."
    - wait: 1200
    - expect: { selector: "#status", contains: "Finished" }
---
Last lesson the counter `i` made the lines grow. A variable can do the same job on its own.

## Predict

```step
stage: predict
code: grow.py#spiral
check:
  type: predict
  q: "Last lesson the spiral used the counter. This one uses size = size + 5. What will it draw?"
  options: ["The same spiral", "A bigger spiral", "A smaller spiral", "An error: size cannot equal size + 5"]
  fault: logic
  misconception: update-is-equation
  actual: "The same spiral. size starts at 0 and grows by 5 on every pass: 0, 5, 10, 15. That is exactly what i * 5 gave last lesson."
```

`size = size + 5` is new. Do you think the spiral will look any different from last lesson's?

## Run

```step
stage: run
code: grow.py#spiral
try: { starter: "grow.py#spiral", height: 420 }
```

Run it and compare it with your prediction.

Here is what each line does.

| Line | What it does | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `size = 0` | Starts `size` at 0 | It is before the loop, so it only happens once |
| `forward(size)` | Draws a line `size` long | Uses whatever `size` holds right now |
| `size = size + 5` | Works out `size + 5`, then stores the answer back in `size` | Read the right side first, then store. It is inside the loop, so it happens every pass |

The picture is the same as last lesson's. There the counter `i` did the growing; here `size` does it.

## Investigate

```step
stage: investigate
code: grow.py#spiral
insight: "A variable can change itself: the right side is worked out first with the old value, and the answer is stored back."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "A program has size = 20. Then it runs the line size = size + 5. What is stored in size afterwards?"
      options: ["25", "5", "20 + 5", "Nothing: the line is an error"]
      answer: 0
      fault: logic
      misconception: update-is-equation
      explain: "Read the line from the right. Python works out size + 5, which is 25, then stores 25 back in size. The = means store, not 'is equal to'."
  - check:
      type: trace
      text: "Fill in the size that forward(size) uses on each pass."
      table: |
        | pass | size used by forward(size) |
        | 1 | 10 |
        | 2 | [20] |
        | 3 | [30] |
        | 4 | [40] |
      explain: "The last line of each pass stores size + 10 back in size, so the next pass starts with a bigger size. This is how a spiral grows."
  - check:
      type: bug
      code: grow.py#bug
      text: "This should draw a growing spiral, but it draws one small square over and over. Click the wrong line."
      answer: 8
      fault: logic
      misconception: update-outside-loop
      explain: "size = size + 5 is not indented, so it runs once, after the loop. Inside the loop it runs on every pass. Indent it under the for line."
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "Last lesson's lines were i * 5. This lesson's size starts at 0. Which update inside the loop gives the same lengths?"
      options: ["size = size + 5", "size = size * 5", "size = i", "size = 5"]
      answer: 0
      explain: "Adding 5 each pass gives 0, 5, 10, 15, the same as i * 5. size * 5 stays at 0, size = i gives 0, 1, 2, and size = 5 is always 5."
```

Follow the value as it changes.

### Store it back

A variable can change itself. The line `size = size + 5` works out `size + 5`, then stores the answer back in `size`.

### Watch it grow

Follow `size` round this loop, which adds to it every pass.

```python
size = 10

for i in range(4):
    forward(size)
    right(90)
    size = size + 10
```

### Spot the bug

An update has to be inside the loop to happen every pass.

### Same lengths, two ways

The counter did this job last lesson. Can `size` do exactly the same?

## Modify

```step
stage: modify
insight: "Changing the amount added changes how fast the value grows, with one edit."
try: { starter: "grow.py#modify", height: 420 }
hint: "Only the number being added needs to change."
check: { type: reflect, text: "I changed the amount added so the spiral grew faster." }
```

Change the amount added each pass so the spiral grows faster. Run it after each change.

## Make

```step
stage: make
try: { starter: "grow.py#make", height: 420 }
hint:
  - "Give the thickness its own variable, like size, and set it before the loop."
  - "Use pensize(width) inside the loop, and add to width at the end of each pass."
check: { type: code, text: "Make the pen thicker every pass using a variable.", rules: { uses: [pensize], loops: 1 } }
smaller:
  check:
    type: trace
    text: "width starts at 2, and each pass draws a line, then adds 2 to width. Fill in the width each line is drawn with."
    table: |
      | pass | width |
      | 1 | 2 |
      | 2 | [4] |
      | 3 | [6] |
      | 5 | [10] |
    explain: "Each pass draws with whatever width holds, then adds 2, so the next line is a bit thicker. That's size = size + 10 again, with a different name."
unlocks: [grow-value]
```

Make the spiral grow **and** get thicker on every pass. The thickness should be a variable that updates itself, like `size` does.

```teacher
summary: Students meet a variable that changes itself, size = size + 5, and use
  it to grow a spiral without the loop counter.
time: 35
timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 5 min · Make 8 min
goals:
  - I can say what size = size + 5 does.
  - I can use an update inside a loop to make a value grow.
  - I can find an update that is in the wrong place.
before: >
  Run the spiral, then make the thickening spiral from the Make step. The key
  line is size = size + 5, which looks wrong to anyone used to maths: in Python
  it means "work out size + 5, then store it back in size". Be ready to say that
  out loud.
running:
  - "Predict: show the spiral and ask whether it looks different from last
    lesson's. The wrong options include an error, because many students think
    size cannot equal size + 5. The counter spiral and the update spiral look
    the same: ask why before running."
  - "Say it aloud: read size = size + 5 right to left. Work out size + 5, then
    store the answer back in size. Say 'store' instead of 'equals'."
  - "Investigate: settle what is stored, trace the value over four passes, then
    show the update outside the loop and ask what happens. The last question
    links back to the counter: two ways to get the same lengths."
  - "Modify: one number changes. Let students predict before they run."
  - "Make: a second variable that updates itself. Students who finish can try
    changing the amount added to the thickness."
stuck:
  - see: The spiral is a square, with every line the same length.
    ask: Does anything change size while the loop runs?
    fix: Add size = size + 5 as the last line inside the loop (indented).
  - see: One small square is drawn over and over.
    ask: Is the update line indented under the for line?
    fix: The update must be inside the loop to run on every pass.
  - see: A student thinks size = size + 5 is an error.
    ask: Which side does Python work out first?
    fix: Work out the right side, then store the answer in the name on the left.
stretch: Make the spiral shrink instead, by subtracting each pass. What happens
  when size goes below 0?
support: Give the trace table with the first two rows filled in and ask the
  student to continue it.
leads: "Next, a street of houses reads a whole program that uses loops, names,
  the counter and updates together. Scores, timers and bank balances all update
  this way. Class ideas: a growing-colour spiral; a countdown."
exit:
  q: What does size = size + 5 do if size is 20?
  a: It works out 20 + 5 = 25 and stores 25 back in size.
explain: >
  `size = size + 5` looks odd, but read it right to left: work out `size + 5`,
  then store the answer back in `size`. That is how a value grows each time
  round a loop.


  Put the update inside the loop and it happens on every pass. Put it after the
  loop and it happens once.


  Last lesson the counter `i` made the lines grow. A variable that updates
  itself does the same job without the counter.
solutions:
  step-4: grow.py#sol-faster
  step-5: grow.py#sol-make
struggle: Reading size = size + 5 as an equation. Have them trace the first
  three values on paper before running it.
class:
  activities:
    - at: start
      kind: info
      title: By the end of this lesson
      do: >
        Here is the finished program running. By the end of the lesson you will
        write one like it.
      notes: Run the finished example on the projector before anything else.
    - at: investigate
      title: Trace size
      minutes: 5
      do: >
        The class calls out size after each pass while one student updates a
        number on the board.
      notes: Make the idea physical before it goes back to the screen.
  self-regulation:
    card: code-trace-it
    mode: show
    at: investigate
    say: "size starts at 10, so I write 10 in my table. Go round once: forward 10,
      then size becomes 15. Round again: forward 15, size becomes 20. I stop
      when I get to the line where my table disagrees with the picture. That's
      where I look."
    notes: Draw the table on the board as you speak. Students listen and watch only;
      the Make step is where they trace for themselves.
```

# region: spiral
from turtle import *

size = 0

for i in range(30):
    forward(size)
    right(90)
    size = size + 5
# endregion

# region: bug
from turtle import *

size = 10

for i in range(30):
    forward(size)
    right(90)
size = size + 5
# endregion

# region: modify
from turtle import *

size = 0

for i in range(30):
    forward(size)
    right(90)
    size = size + 5

# Change the amount added so the spiral grows faster.
# endregion

# region: make
from turtle import *

size = 0

for i in range(30):
    forward(size)
    right(90)
    size = size + 5
    # Make the pen thicker every pass too.
# endregion

# region: sol-faster
from turtle import *

size = 0

for i in range(30):
    forward(size)
    right(90)
    size = size + 10
# endregion

# region: sol-make
from turtle import *

size = 0
width = 1

for i in range(30):
    pensize(width)
    forward(size)
    right(90)
    size = size + 5
    width = width + 0.5
# endregion
